figures.caption: Table 1: Generative neural foundation models. “Backbone” is Transformer (Tr.), state-space model (SSM), or U-Net. “Obj.” is the objective: autoregressive (AR), masked reconstruction (MR), or flow matching (FM). “Data” is the pre-training corpus duration in hours; “Ch.” the number of input channels (parcels for source-space models); “Rate” the sampling rate of the model input; “Params” the largest pre-trained variant reported; “Compute” the reported pre-training cost in GPU-hours (GPU types differ between papers). “–” denotes not reported; † marks papers that report the GPU type and count but not the training time.

Figure 1: Overview of MEG-Mamba. A) Continuous source reconstructed, parcellated MEG data are mapped to a sequence of discrete tokens by a learned tokeniser model. B) MEG-Mamba is an autoregressive foundation model that predicts the next token (each parcel is modelled independently); the backbone stacks N=4 Mamba-3 blocks.

Figure 2: Training dynamics and scalability. A) Cross entropy (left) and next-token top-1 accuracy (middle) on the training and held-out sets over epochs. The small generalisation gap (right) indicates negligible overfitting. B) Pre-training cost (left) and context length (right) of MEG-Mamba and MEG-GPT.

Figure 3: MEG-Mamba learns meaningful embeddings. PCA projections of the learned embeddings. A) Session embeddings encode participant age. B) Parcel embeddings recover the spatial organisation of the cortex: parcels cluster by cortical region (frontal, central, parietal, temporal, occipital).

Figure 4: MEG-Mamba produces realistic, high-fidelity synthetic MEG data. Data are generated for held-out subjects; their spatio-spectral characteristics (A, B) and dynamics (C) closely match real data. A) Power spectral densities of each parcel for real (left) and generated (middle) data, and real versus generated band power for each parcel (right). B) Relative power maps for each canonical band. C) Wavelet time-frequency representation of 30 s of real and generated data at an occipital parcel.

Figure 5: MEG-Mamba reproduces task-evoked responses for held-out subjects. Trial-averaged time-frequency responses (log-ratio baseline, dB; shown from −0.5 to 1 s) of real data (left) and data generated by the stimulus-conditioned model (Section 4.3; right), for visual stimuli (top; left primary visual cortex), button presses (middle; left primary motor cortex), and auditory stimuli (bottom; right primary auditory cortex), in the 62 subjects held out of pre-training and fine-tuning. Generated data recover the characteristic evoked spectral patterns.
